repo.description:
### Summary
code-server's session cookie could be read by services opened through the built-in port proxy. The cookie was sent to the proxied service on WebSocket connections, and because it was not marked `HttpOnly`, scripts on proxied pages could read it. The cookie acts as a reusable credential, so anyone who obtains it can sign in to code-server as the user.

### Details
code-server removes its session cookie from requests it forwards to proxied ports. This was only done for regular HTTP requests. WebSocket connections through `/proxy/<port>/`, `/absproxy/<port>/` and the proxy domain still sent the full `Cookie` header, including the session cookie, to the proxied service. Versions before `4.124.2` also sent the cookie on regular HTTP requests.

Separately, the session cookie was set without the `HttpOnly` attribute. Pages served through the path proxy share the code-server origin, so scripts on those pages could read the cookie with `document.cookie`.

### Impact
A malicious service listening on a port that the user opens through the proxy can capture the session cookie and replay it to get full access to code-server, including the terminal and file system, as the user running code-server. To exploit this, the attacker has to control a service reachable by the proxy, and a signed-in user has to open it.

### Patches
Fixed in 4.145.0. The session cookie is now removed from proxied WebSocket connections and is set with `HttpOnly`. Upgrade to 4.145.0 or later.

### Workarounds
Only open trusted services through the code-server proxy. After upgrading, change the code-server password if you previously opened untrusted services through the proxy, since this invalidates any session cookie that may have been captured.

### References
- https://github.com/coder/code-server/pull/8111
- https://github.com/coder/code-server/pull/8110
- https://github.com/coder/code-server/releases/tag/v4.145.0

### Credits
Thanks to @j9tdsn8nmk-hash, @bl4cksku11 and @Iraianbu-tech for reporting this issue.
repo.summary: Session cookie exposed to services opened through the port proxy
